title: From algorithmic personalization to informational wars: The dynamics of (dis)information bubbles around the september 7, 2021
screen_reason: Portuguese-language Twitter study (search term '7 de setembro', 1-8 September 2021, 40,000 tweets). Beyond the network analysis, section 3.4 content-analyses the news items reached through the most-shared URLs and reports verbatim shares classified as fabricated news and hoaxes against Rubin, Chen and Conroy's (2016) typology, with counts and denominators, broken down by outlet type (traditional 100% genuine n=1,774; independent 90% genuine n=410 / 10% fabricated n=46; partisan 61% genuine n=1,681 / 23% fabricated n=634 / 11% hoaxes n=312). Those are quantitative falsity shares of shared link occurrences with a stated denominator.

estimates.platform: Twitter (links to partisan media outlets shared in tweets)
estimates.date: 1-8 September 2021 (8 days, 5,000 tweets sampled per day)
estimates.measure_type: % of shared-link occurrences pointing to partisan media outlets whose news item was classified as fabricated news
estimates.value_raw: 23% de notícias tipificadas como fabricadas (n = 634) [23% of news typified as fabricated (n = 634)]; partisan-outlet occurrences 1,681 genuine + 634 fabricated + 312 hoaxes + 138 unavailable = 2,765
estimates.denominator: 2,765 occurrences of shared links pointing to the 24 partisan media outlets, among the 4,995 occurrences of the 170 URLs (47 distinct outlets) that were shared at least 10 times in the 40,000-tweet corpus
estimates.definition: the news item reached by the shared link was coded “notícias fabricadas” (fabricated news) per Rubin, Chen and Conroy (2016): fraudulent reporting, yellow press and tabloids presenting unverified news with clickbait headlines, exaggeration, scandal-mongering or sensationalism
estimates.misinfo_def: "Notícias fabricadas: “reportagens fraudulentas” […], a imprensa marrom e os tablóides apresentam um amplo espectro de notícias não verificadas e usam manchetes atraentes (“caça-cliques”), exageros, escândalos ou sensacionalismo para aumentar o tráfego ou os lucros” (RUBIN; CHEN; CONROY, 2016, p. 3, tradução nossa)" [EN, the paper's own footnote of the original: "fraudulent reporting [...], yellow press and tabloids present a wide spectrum of unverified new and uses eye-catching headlines ('clickbaits'), exaggerations, scandal-mongering, or sensationalism to increase traffic or profits"]
estimates.source_quote: Já os meios de comunicação classificados como partidários apresentaram 61% de notícias genuínas (n = 1681), 23% de notícias tipificadas como fabricadas (n = 634), e 11% de embustes (n = 312); 5% não estavam disponíveis para consulta, com acesso restrito apenas para assinantes (n = 138).
estimates.ground_truth_detail: The two authors' content analysis, applying Rubin, Chen and Conroy's (2016) three-way typology (genuine news / fabricated news / hoaxes) to the news items behind each shared URL; outlets separately typed as traditional, independent or partisan (Holt et al. 2019; Beers 2006; Weeks 2017). No inter-coder reliability statistic is reported, and the paper lists possible misclassification among its limitations.
estimates.moderator_quote: Dos 170 URLs analisados, foram identificadas 47 diferentes fontes de comunicação, sendo a prevalência (51,0%) de compartilhamento de informações oriundas de meios de comunicação partidários (n = 24), seguido de 27,6% de fontes de meios de comunicação tradicionais (n = 13) e 21,3% de fontes caracterizadas como independentes (n = 10).
estimates.notes: EN translation of the source quote: 'Media outlets classified as partisan showed 61% genuine news (n = 1,681), 23% of news typified as fabricated (n = 634), and 11% hoaxes (n = 312); 5% were not available for consultation, restricted to subscribers (n = 138).' Coded SHARING/content_share because the denominator is occurrences of links SHARED in the tweet corpus (4,995 occurrences of 170 URLs), not an outlet's complete output; an adjudicator could argue CONTENT if the occurrences are read as items rather than share events, but the paper counts co-occurrences in tweets. denom_scope=topical (single search term '7 de setembro'); denom_selection=curated because only URLs with >= 10 co-occurrences entered the analysis. topic=politics_elections is the nearest code for an anti-democratic political mobilisation around Brazil's Independence Day (not an election campaign). The 2,765 denominator is the sum of the four verbatim category counts; the VALUE (23%) is verbatim, so R8 is satisfied. Do NOT add 23% + 11% into a 34% total: that cross-category sum is forbidden by R8, though it means the true partisan-outlet falsity share exceeds 23%.

estimates.notes: Flagged definition_variant=true: this is the same denominator as the previous row under a second, mutually exclusive falsity label (hoaxes rather than fabricated news). It must NOT be pooled additively with the 23% row, and the 34% total the two imply cannot be kept under R8 (cross-category sum). Kept so that an adjudicator sees that the paper's partisan-outlet falsity coding covers two categories, not one.

estimates.notes: EN translation: 'As regards the analysis of news published by independent media outlets, 90% of the news was genuine (n = 410), while 10% was fabricated news (n = 46).' Denominator 456 = 410 + 46 (verbatim counts, same denominator, so R8's part/whole allowance applies); the value 10% is itself verbatim.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) Traditional media: 'identificou-se que 100% das noticias divulgadas por meio de links de meios de comunicacao categorizados como tradicionais consistia em noticias genuinas (n = 1.774)' ['100% of the news disseminated through links from outlets categorised as traditional consisted of genuine news (n = 1,774)']. This implies a 0% falsity share for traditional-media links (n = 1,774 occurrences), but 0% would be a complement I computed, which R8 forbids, so no row was written. An adjudicator may wish to add it as a legitimate 0/1,774. (2) No pooled falsity share across all 4,995 occurrences is reported, and no share of the 40,000 tweets is coded for falsity, so there is no whole-corpus prevalence estimate. (3) Bot and hashtag figures are not misinformation shares and were not extracted: 48.6% (n=36) of 74 top-outdegree superparticipant accounts were bots, 44.6% (n=33) human, 6.8% (n=5) suspended; 77.8% (n=28) of the 36 political bots were pro-far-right and 22.2% (n=8) pro-left; 17.3% (n=6,922) of tweets contained a hashtag; 23.8% (n=9,508) contained a URL; 51.0% (n=24) of the 47 outlets were partisan, 27.6% (n=13) traditional, 21.3% (n=10) independent; 83.3% (n=20) of partisan outlets were pro-far-right. The abstract's headline percentages (77.8% and 83.3%) are of these kinds, i.e. bot/outlet composition, not misinformation prevalence. (4) The paper reports that the pro-far-right bubble concentrated the highest-indegree nodes on six of eight days, but gives no top-X%/share-of-activity pair, so R1 rules out a CONCENTRATION row. (5) Figura 4 (the type-of-information x outlet-type chart) is an image and is not present in the text file; all values above come from the narrative, which is why confidence is medium.

rob.design: Twitter API keyword collection on '7 de setembro', 1-8 September 2021, capped at 5,000 tweets per day (40,000 total: 5,830 originals, 34,170 retweets); no probability sample of the day's tweets and the daily cap is not explained. Network analysis in Gephi (Louvain modularity, ForceAtlas2) with bubble labels assigned by the authors from account metadata; bots identified by two detectors (Pegabot and Botometer) plus a final manual check. Falsity coding is a content analysis of the 170 URLs with >= 10 co-occurrences (47 outlets, 4,995 occurrences) using Rubin, Chen and Conroy's (2016) genuine/fabricated/hoax typology; the number of coders, the coding protocol and any inter-coder reliability are not reported, and the authors list possible misclassification as a limitation. Falsity is judged for the item behind the link, but the outlet-type strata mean much of the signal is outlet-driven.
